rich.text: (Bereshit) — אֲבָל בְּשַׁבָּת סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם אִתְפְּרִיסָא עַל עָלְמָא... וּבְגִין כָּךְ בִּקְדוּשָּׁא דְיוֹמָא מְבָרְכִינָן הַפּוֹרֵס סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל כָּל עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַםִ: "On Shabbat the shelter of peace is spread over the world... therefore in the holiness of the day we bless 'Who spreads the shelter of peace over us, over all His people Israel, and over Jerusalem.'" The Zohar continues (78:194): אַמַּאי עַל יְרוּשָׁלָם, אֶלָּא דָא הִיא מְדוֹרָא דְהַהִיא סֻכָּה — Jerusalem is the dwelling of that shelter. This is the basis for his opening: on Shabbat all Israel merit the holiness of Yerushalayim and the Mikdash.

p: And this is the depth of the words of
the question of the holy Zohar
"'[This stone] shall be the house of God' (Bereishis 28:22) —
it should have said 'the house of Hashem,'
'Let us go to the house of Hashem,' etc." (Tehillim 122:1).
So too the Midrash Rabbah was troubled:
אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם בֵּית ה'.
"this is none other than the house of Hashem."
that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed
and then it is called "the house of Hashem,"
that the dread of Hashem and the fear fall
it is not manifest that it is awesome,
that the dread of Hashem falls
since they shriek in His sanctuary;
and then it is not called "the house of Hashem"
the dread of Hashem from the Beit HaMikdash,
the Men of the Great Assembly:
"and this is the gate of heaven" —
and on this the Midrash Rabbah brings:
'For He has strengthened the bars of your gates,'"
Rather, the main point is that it expounded
"and this is the gate of heaven"
as referring to [the Temple] built and perfected
the Matnos Kehunah from the Yalkut.
And this is the meaning of
"and this is the gate of heaven":
will be built by the hands of Heaven
and will descend built and perfected,
And this is the meaning of
"and this is the gate of heaven" —
built and perfected in the time to come:
this is the Beit HaMikdash above,
which will descend built and perfected.
And this is what they showed Yaakov.

p: And regarding Shabbat it is written:
and to visit in His sanctuary" (Tehillim 27:4);
for then Hashem, may He be blessed,
spreads the shelter of peace over us, etc.,
and this comes through the attribute of
Yaakov our forefather, peace be upon him.
And this is what is said of Yaakov:
"And he looked, and behold, a well in the field,"
the level of "the Lord of all the earth,"
As written in the holy Zohar
that Yaakov is the supernal chariot,
from the spring of all springs —
as written in the holy Zohar;
And of Moshe it is written:
the image of the central pillar
Rather, he was from the inside —
and that one from the soul."
That is, Moshe is the soul,
Therefore it is written of him,
for he was "the man of God,"
and the Holy One, blessed be He,
as it were, would fulfill it.
And it is mentioned seven times,
indicating that he is in wholeness,
that he radiates to Knesses Yisrael
And this is the attribute of "awesome":
so that it enters the depths of the heart.

rich.text: (Vayetzei) — בְּמֹשֶׁה לָא כְּתִיב אֶלָּא זִמְנָא חֲדָא... בְּגִין דְּמֹשֶׁה כַּד עָאל אִתְפְּרַשׁ מִכֹּל וָכֹל מִבֵּיתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְיַעֲקֹב לָא אִתְפְּרַשׁ כְּלָל... וּבְגִין כָּךְ מֹשֶׁה מָארֵיהּ דְּבֵיתָא הֲוָה... בְּמֹשֶׁה כְּתִיב וַיֵּשֶׁב עַל הַבְּאֵר, בְּיַעֲקֹב וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה בְאֵר. This is the passage behind his contrast: Moshe, master of the house, 'sat by the well' (once); Yaakov 'saw the well' (seven times). He does not name it; it comes right after the seven-wells passage.

rich.text: (Vaera) — מֹשֶׁה אִלְמָלֵא דַּהֲוָה מָארֵיהּ דְּבֵיתָא אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים אִתְעֲנַשׁ עַל מַה דְּאָמַר: "Had Moshe not been master of the house, man of God, he would have been punished." The Zohar uses this phrase for Moshe in several places (also Zohar I 152b, in the note above).
